subject: ACME pricing & invoice estimate — follow-up and token volumes
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: ACME pricing & invoice estimate — follow-up and token volumes

Tom — great to meet this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call:

Summary / ask:
- Primary use case: in-product summarization + conversational assistants for customer support (short + long form generation). Embeddings for semantic search in new knowledge base.
- Questions we still need to finalize pricing and an official estimate: monthly token volumes (generation + embeddings), expected peak concurrency, and target $/1M-token you’re aiming for in year 1. Also confirm whether you need a dedicated (reserved) capacity quote or hosted API for initial rollout.

Attached I’ve dropped a preliminary invoice estimate and the Redwood pricing calculator (two tabs: conservative and aggressive assumptions). The attached workbook uses your rough numbers from the call to show per-month invoice ranges and a 12-month committed scenario with discounts.

Immediate next steps:
1) If you can provide a simple monthly token projection (by feature: convo gen, async batch gen, embeddings) I’ll produce an updated invoice and a 1-page unit economics summary.
2) If helpful, we can lock a short 30-min follow-up next week to walk the cost model and finalize a draft SOW. Please send preferred times.

Target questions I asked on the call (copying here so we have it in thread):
- Baseline monthly tokens: ?
- Burst/peak: ?
- Target $/1M tokens you’re budgeting for (or monthly budget range): ?

Files attached: ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_20261120.xlsx; redwood_pricing_calculator_v2.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll stand by to update the estimate once I have the volumes.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0138
https://redwoodinference.com

From: Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Natalie Perez <natalie.perez@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME pricing & invoice estimate — follow-up and token volumes

Sean — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. Quick answers below and attached our projected usage CSV.

Baseline monthly projection (first 6 months):
- Conversational generation (short): 12M tokens/month
- Conversational generation (long): 8M tokens/month
- Async batch generation (reports): 5M tokens/month
- Embeddings (semantic search + KB): 10M tokens/month
Total: ~35M tokens/month (generation + embeddings).

Peak/burst: expect up to 3x baseline during product launches; typical spikes 2–6 hours/day.

Budget/target: we’re looking to land at approximately $2K–$3K per 1M tokens as a blended target for year 1 (we know that’s broad). Our procurement team has an initial budget range of $80k–$120k/month for inference costs, excluding infra ops.

We attached ACME_usage_projection_20261120.csv with feature-level rows and month-by-month projections. Happy to go through your calc. We’d prefer a hosted start but would consider dedicated/reserved if pricing and SLA justify it.

Best,
Tom Li
Head of Platform Product
Acme Corp

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 10:15 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Tom — great to meet this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call:...

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME pricing & invoice estimate — follow-up and token volumes

Thanks Tom — this is really helpful. I updated the attached estimate based on your projections and sketched two scenarios below. I’ve also added a conservative committed-discount path if you sign up for a 12-month reserved commit.

High-level invoice estimate (rounded):
- Scenario A (Hosted, pay-as-you-go, blended): ~35M tokens/month -> estimated $70k–$105k/month (blended $2K–$3K per 1M tokens)
- Scenario B (12-month commit with volume discount): -> estimated $56k–$84k/month (effective $1.6K–$2.4K per 1M tokens)

Unit economics detail (examples):
- Generation (autoregressive) effective compute cost estimate: $XXX per 1M tokens (depends on model and quantization)
- Embeddings (sparse) effective compute cost estimate: $YYY per 1M tokens
- Platform + routing + cache savings baked in to blended price above

Notes / assumptions baked into the attached calc:
- Model: mix of open LLMs (gpt-like) with quantization on dedicated pools for commit pricing.
- 20% headroom for burst capacity in hosted scenario (affects peak unit costs).
- 30% discount applied in committed scenario as an example — we can run custom sensitivities.

Attachments: updated ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_20261120.xlsx (tab: 'ACME_final_estimate') and link to cost model: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_redwood_acme_cost_model

Next steps:
- If the committed scenario looks attractive I’ll put together a formal quote and a draft SOW for procurement.
- Can we set a 30-min review early next week? I have availability Tue/Wed 9–11am PST.

If you’d like I can also run a quick sensitivity that shows price per 1M tokens by model family (smaller models vs larger models) so procurement can see tradeoffs.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0138

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: ACME pricing & invoice estimate — follow-up and token volumes

Team — forwarding Acme thread and the updated estimator. Tom’s baseline is ~35M tokens/mo and procurement is targeting $2K–$3K per 1M tokens. They’re open to start hosted but will consider committed reserved if economics hit the lower band.

Action items for us:
- Monica: can you draft a formal quote (show both hosted and committed 12mo commit) with the two scenarios (list price + 20% and committed discount) and include a short playbook on how caching/batching can reduce effective cost? Use the updated spreadsheet attached.
- Rafael: please prepare a note on SLA/throughput for 3x burst and check whether we need to propose burst credits or a dedicated capacity add-on.

Timeline: Sean to share draft quote by EOD Monday so I can hand to procurement.

Forwarded message below.

Thanks,
Sean
